content: Instead of envying the young for their possibilities, the old person can look with pride on the realities he has achieved, the values he has actualized, and the suffering he has borne.
author: Viktor Frankl
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Viktor Frankl understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
